sentences.text: Over ten years, stocks outgrew homes almost nine times in ten.
sentences.spoken: Over ten years, stocks outgrew homes almost nine times in ten.

sentences.text: So renting looks smart. Nina rents, with $92,000 saved.
sentences.spoken: So renting looks smart. Nina rents, with ninety-two thousand dollars saved.

sentences.text: If her renting twin held cash, her buying twin ended ahead about 3 in 4 times.
sentences.spoken: If her renting twin held cash, her buying twin ended ahead about three in four times.

sentences.text: With that cash in stocks instead, the buyer led only about half the time.
sentences.spoken: With that cash in stocks instead, the buyer led only about half the time.

sentences.text: Over fifteen years, cash kept the buyer ahead every time; stocks, only about 1 in 5.
sentences.spoken: Over fifteen years, cash kept the buyer ahead every time; stocks, only about one in five.

sentences.text: So if Nina rents and invests the difference, does she end up ahead of owning?
sentences.spoken: [worried] So if Nina rents and invests the difference, does she end up ahead of owning?

sentences.text: Stocks outgrew the house almost nine times out of ten, yet buying still came out ahead in half.
sentences.spoken: Stocks outgrew the house almost nine times out of ten, yet buying still came out ahead in half.

sentences.text: It's history, not a forecast.
sentences.spoken: It's history, not a forecast.

sentences.text: We replayed every start month since 1991 as a house on one long street: lit if the buyer ends ahead, dark if not.
sentences.spoken: We replayed every start month since nineteen ninety-one as a house on one long street: lit if the buyer ends ahead, dark if not.

sentences.text: The renting twin's pile is the $92,000, plus whatever owning would have cost each month beyond her rent.
sentences.spoken: The renting twin's pile is the ninety-two thousand dollars, plus whatever owning would have cost each month beyond her rent.

sentences.text: All of it goes into the whole US stock market, every month, through every drop.
sentences.spoken: All of it goes into the whole U.S. stock market, every month, through every drop.

sentences.text: The first house on that street is January 1991.
sentences.spoken: The first house on that street is January nineteen ninety-one.

sentences.text: With the renting twin's pile kept in cash, the buyer finished ten years $48,410 ahead.
sentences.spoken: With the renting twin's pile kept in cash, the buyer finished ten years forty-eight thousand four hundred ten dollars ahead.

sentences.text: With the pile in stocks, the same buyer finished $485,063 behind.
sentences.spoken: With the pile in stocks, the same buyer finished four hundred eighty-five thousand sixty-three dollars behind.

sentences.text: Same house, same mortgage, same rent; the only thing that moved was the renter's pile.
sentences.spoken: Same house, same mortgage, same rent; the only thing that moved was the renter's pile.

sentences.text: In those ten years, a dollar in the whole US stock market grew almost five times.
sentences.spoken: In those ten years, a dollar in the whole U.S. stock market grew almost five times.

sentences.text: And the renter's pile was never a single dollar: it was the $92,000 on day one, plus a deposit every month.
sentences.spoken: And the renter's pile was never a single dollar: it was the ninety-two thousand dollars on day one, plus a deposit every month.

sentences.text: Whenever owning cost more than renting that month, the gap went into her pile, and the market grew that too.
sentences.spoken: Whenever owning cost more than renting that month, the gap went into her pile, and the market grew that too.

sentences.text: So one change, stocks instead of cash, turned the first house from lit to dark.
sentences.spoken: So one change, stocks instead of cash, turned the first house from lit to dark.

sentences.text: A lot of rent-versus-buy math assumes one growth rate; this replays what actually happened, month by month.
sentences.spoken: A lot of rent-versus-buy math assumes one growth rate; this replays what actually happened, month by month.

sentences.text: The renting twin's rent is an assumption, the tag on her door: 5 percent of the price a year, as of July 2026, and later, that tag decides.
sentences.spoken: The renting twin's rent is an assumption, the tag on her door: five percent of the price a year, as of July twenty twenty-six, and later, that tag decides.

sentences.text: So, with the pile in stocks, how much of the street stays lit?
sentences.spoken: So, with the pile in stocks, how much of the street stays lit?

sentences.text: After ten years, a house is lit if the buying twin's equity, after selling costs, is bigger than the renting twin's pile.
sentences.spoken: After ten years, a house is lit if the buying twin's equity, after selling costs, is bigger than the renting twin's pile.

sentences.text: If the pile is bigger, the door goes dark.
sentences.spoken: If the pile is bigger, the door goes dark.

sentences.text: That's 307 houses, from January 1991 to the last start with ten full years of data, July 2016.
sentences.spoken: That's three hundred seven houses, from January nineteen ninety-one to the last start with ten full years of data, July twenty sixteen.

sentences.text: Nina's own month isn't on the street; its ten years are still ahead of her.
sentences.spoken: Nina's own month isn't on the street; its ten years are still ahead of her.

sentences.text: About two in three of the 1990s houses stay lit.
sentences.spoken: About two in three of the 1990s houses stay lit.

sentences.text: But the darkest house on the whole street is the very first one.
sentences.spoken: But the darkest house on the whole street is the very first one.

sentences.text: Its renting twin caught the long stock boom from its first month.
sentences.spoken: Its renting twin caught the long stock boom from its first month.

sentences.text: A few years later, the market itself stalled.
sentences.spoken: A few years later, the market itself stalled.

sentences.text: For a short run of start months, a dollar in stocks was worth less than a dollar ten years on.
sentences.spoken: For a short run of start months, a dollar in stocks was worth less than a dollar ten years on.

sentences.text: Those houses stay lit: the pile lost ground while the buyer kept paying down her loan.
sentences.spoken: Those houses stay lit: the pile lost ground while the buyer kept paying down her loan.

sentences.text: Then the street goes dark, and stays dark.
sentences.spoken: Then the street goes dark, and stays dark.

sentences.text: For houses bought in the bubble years, the buyer ended ahead in none of them.
sentences.spoken: For houses bought in the bubble years, the buyer ended ahead in none of them.

sentences.text: With cash, some of them had stayed lit; with stocks, those lights go out too.
sentences.spoken: With cash, some of them had stayed lit; with stocks, those lights go out too.

sentences.text: These buyers paid near the peak of home prices, while their twins kept buying stocks through the market's fall and rebound.
sentences.spoken: These buyers paid near the peak of home prices, while their twins kept buying stocks through the market's fall and rebound.

sentences.text: Last time, with the pile in cash, the darkest house was one bought near the top.
sentences.spoken: Last time, with the pile in cash, the darkest house was one bought near the top.

sentences.text: With stocks, that buyer ends more than a quarter of a million dollars behind.
sentences.spoken: With stocks, that buyer ends more than a quarter of a million dollars behind.

sentences.text: The dark house got darker.
sentences.spoken: The dark house got darker.

sentences.text: Dark doors don't mean the renting twins had an easy ride.
sentences.spoken: Dark doors don't mean the renting twins had an easy ride.

sentences.text: Along the way, many of the stock piles dipped below where they started.
sentences.spoken: Along the way, many of the stock piles dipped below where they started.

sentences.text: One renting twin's pile sank to $54,310, and she kept investing.
sentences.spoken: [serious] One renting twin's pile sank to fifty-four thousand three hundred ten dollars, and she kept investing.

sentences.text: The replay assumes every renting twin did exactly that, every month, through every drop.
sentences.spoken: The replay assumes every renting twin did exactly that, every month, through every drop.

sentences.text: Real people sometimes stop, and a renter who sells in a crash is not on this street.
sentences.spoken: Real people sometimes stop, and a renter who sells in a crash is not on this street.

sentences.text: So, after the whole walk, how many houses are lit?
sentences.spoken: So, after the whole walk, how many houses are lit?

sentences.text: Lit: 152 of the 307, about half.
sentences.spoken: Lit: one hundred fifty-two of the three hundred seven, about half.

sentences.text: Every house that changed sides went from the buyer to the renter, never the other way.
sentences.spoken: Every house that changed sides went from the buyer to the renter, never the other way.

sentences.text: That half is a count of what already happened, not a promise about Nina's month.
sentences.spoken: That half is a count of what already happened, not a promise about Nina's month.

sentences.text: The brightest house last time still glows.
sentences.spoken: The brightest house last time still glows.

sentences.text: With stocks, that buyer still ends well ahead.
sentences.spoken: With stocks, that buyer still ends well ahead.

sentences.text: She bought after prices had fallen, and her house rose on its whole price, not just on her $92,000.
sentences.spoken: She bought after prices had fallen, and her house rose on its whole price, not just on her ninety-two thousand dollars.

sentences.text: In the years after the crash, most of the lights come back on.
sentences.spoken: In the years after the crash, most of the lights come back on.

sentences.text: So the half isn't spread evenly: whole stretches are lit, and one long stretch is dark.
sentences.spoken: So the half isn't spread evenly: whole stretches are lit, and one long stretch is dark.

sentences.text: Those buyers started with lower prices and low mortgage rates, and that held the lights on.
sentences.spoken: Those buyers started with lower prices and low mortgage rates, and that held the lights on.

sentences.text: Over a shorter stay, with the pile in stocks, the buyer was ahead a little more than half the time.
sentences.spoken: Over a shorter stay, with the pile in stocks, the buyer was ahead a little more than half the time.

sentences.text: In this replay, the longer the stay, the more often the pile finished ahead.
sentences.spoken: In this replay, the longer the stay, the more often the pile finished ahead.

sentences.text: Half a street, lit in stretches; now, a longer stay.
sentences.spoken: Half a street, lit in stretches; now, a longer stay.

sentences.text: Stay longer still, and with stocks, most of the lights go out.
sentences.spoken: Stay longer still, and with stocks, most of the lights go out.

sentences.text: With cash, every one of the 247 fifteen-year starts left the buyer ahead.
sentences.spoken: With cash, every one of the two hundred forty-seven fifteen-year starts left the buyer ahead.

sentences.text: With stocks, only about one in five did.
sentences.spoken: With stocks, only about one in five did.

sentences.text: The longer the stay, the longer the pile has to compound, and the further it pulls ahead.
sentences.spoken: The longer the stay, the longer the pile has to compound, and the further it pulls ahead.

sentences.text: Longer stays favored the pile; the rent tag is the one assumption left to test.
sentences.spoken: Longer stays favored the pile; the rent tag is the one assumption left to test.

sentences.text: So how can stocks outgrow home prices about 9 in 10 times, and the buyer still finish ahead in half?
sentences.spoken: So how can stocks outgrow home prices about nine in ten times, and the buyer still finish ahead in half?

sentences.text: Because the buyer's house grows on all $400,000 of it, while the renter's pile starts at $92,000.
sentences.spoken: Because the buyer's house grows on all four hundred thousand dollars of it, while the renter's pile starts at ninety-two thousand dollars.

sentences.text: The mortgage lets a slower thing grow on a much bigger base.
sentences.spoken: The mortgage lets a slower thing grow on a much bigger base.

sentences.text: The renter catches up only through the monthly gap, and through time.
sentences.spoken: The renter catches up only through the monthly gap, and through time.

sentences.text: So what if nobody saves that gap, and only the $92,000 is invested?
sentences.spoken: So what if nobody saves that gap, and only the ninety-two thousand dollars is invested?

sentences.text: Then the buyer is ahead in about 2 in 3 start months.
sentences.spoken: Then the buyer is ahead in about two in three start months.

sentences.text: The monthly habit, not the one big deposit, did most of the renter's catching up.
sentences.spoken: The monthly habit, not the one big deposit, did most of the renter's catching up.

sentences.text: The pile in this replay also pays no fees and no taxes.
sentences.spoken: The pile in this replay also pays no fees and no taxes.

sentences.text: With 1 percent a year taken out, the lit share rises to 55 percent.
sentences.spoken: With one percent a year taken out, the lit share rises to fifty-five percent.

sentences.text: Each real cost on the renter's side moves houses back toward the buyer.
sentences.spoken: Each real cost on the renter's side moves houses back toward the buyer.

sentences.text: And then there's the tag on Nina's door.
sentences.spoken: And then there's the tag on Nina's door.

sentences.text: At 5 percent, the street splits almost exactly in half.
sentences.spoken: At five percent, the street splits almost exactly in half.

sentences.text: The split sits near 5.1 percent, and public rent data from the Census Bureau falls on both sides of it.
sentences.spoken: The split sits near five point one percent, and public rent data from the Census Bureau falls on both sides of it.

sentences.text: So the answer sits on the rent tag, and the tag is an assumption.
sentences.spoken: So the answer sits on the rent tag, and the tag is an assumption.

sentences.text: None of this ranks stocks above a house, or a house above stocks.
sentences.spoken: None of this ranks stocks above a house, or a house above stocks.

sentences.text: A home is also stability and control, and no street of numbers counts those.
sentences.spoken: A home is also stability and control, and no street of numbers counts those.

sentences.text: The rest of the limits are on the card: US only, history, not a forecast, no taxes on gains or on the home, and renters who never skip a month.
sentences.spoken: The rest of the limits are on the card: U.S. only, history, not a forecast, no taxes on gains or on the home, and renters who never skip a month.

sentences.text: So, back to Nina's question.
sentences.spoken: So, back to Nina's question.

sentences.text: With the pile in cash, most of her street was lit; in stocks, about half; over fifteen years, most of it dark.
sentences.spoken: With the pile in cash, most of her street was lit; in stocks, about half; over fifteen years, most of it dark.

sentences.text: It's the same street as at the start, read again with the pile in the market.
sentences.spoken: It's the same street as at the start, read again with the pile in the market.

sentences.text: What no house on this street can show is how long Nina herself will stay.
sentences.spoken: What no house on this street can show is how long Nina herself will stay.

sentences.text: Nina's answer: investing the difference made her street a coin flip, and her rent tag tips it.
sentences.spoken: [thoughtful] Nina's answer: investing the difference made her street a coin flip, and her rent tag tips it.
